ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 31 October 2006; revised 8 November 2024; effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (State Administration for Market Regulation and People's Bank of China Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Administrative Measures for the Reporting of Large-Value and Suspicious Transactions (PBOC Order [2016] No. 3); Measures on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Supervision for Financial Institutions and Specific Non-Financial Institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent registrar in the parent entity's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: notarization at the origin notary public, then Apostille by the designated competent authority if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member; Consular Legalization path only: notarization at the origin notary public, then legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate in the origin state if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registry authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only for Apostille Convention member states; Consular Legalization only for non-member states. Notarization is required before either path, but Apostille and Consular Legalization must never be applied sequentially to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the parent entity authorizing incorporation of the WFOE and appointing the local representative or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the parent entity, notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states, attach the notarized board resolution and a Hague Apostille only; for non-Convention states, attach the notarized board resolution and a PRC consular legalization only. These routes are mutually exclusive alternatives and must not be chained together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (charter) of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or legal representative of the parent entity, certified by the parent entity and notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route only: notarization followed by Apostille from the origin country's competent authority; non-Apostille route only: notarization followed by consular legalization from the PRC Embassy/Consulate in the origin country. No sequential use of both authentication regimes is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate parent entity's corporate bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate bank or financial institution where the parent entity maintains its principal account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states, the bank letter must be notarized in origin and then attached with a Hague Apostille only; for non-member states, the bank letter must be notarized in origin and then submitted to PRC consular legalization only. The two mechanisms are exclusive and cannot be combined in a single chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any engagement, all legal representatives, directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories and senior EOR payroll personnel must be screened continuously against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and PRC's Unreliable Entity List and Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law designations. PEP status, including domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and close associates, must be verified through independent data sources and risk-ranked. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where a PEP, politically exposed shareholder, or sanctions-linked jurisdiction is identified, including source-of-wealth documentation and senior management sign-off before proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Enterprise Name Registration Declaration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR National Integrated Enterprise Registration Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be written in standardized simplified Chinese characters and must follow the statutory four-tier formula: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and the statutory limited liability company organizational-form token. Pinyin and traditional Chinese are not acceptable as the registered Chinese name. A foreign investor may separately show its transliterated or original foreign name in the English version of the business license. The distinctive name must not violate public order, false-advertising prohibitions, or trademark rights, and the industry term must correspond to the approved business scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name system rejects an application, the applicant must download the written rejection notice and, within 30 days, submit an administrative reconsideration application to the rejecting SAMR office or the higher-level market regulation department under the Administrative Reconsideration Law. The appeal must state the application number, the rejected name, legal grounds, and include comparison tables of similar approved names. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may institute administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months after the reconsideration decision is served.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not acceptable for WFOE registration, tax registration, payroll licensing, or corporate bank account opening under current SAMR, tax, and PBOC practice. The registered address must be a physically occupied, leasable office space in mainland China, evidenced by a lease contract, real estate ownership certificate, and site photographs. Some Pilot Free Trade Zones, such as Shanghai FTZ, Qianhai, and Hengqin, permit cluster registration under special local rules, but such arrangements are still subject to strict substance review and are generally rejected for labor dispatch or human resources service licensure and for payroll bank accounts. For an ISIC 7810 global EOR staffing agency, substantive local presence is effectively mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is high, approximately 75 to 85 percent within the first 12 months after obtaining the Human Resources Service License or Labor Dispatch Administrative License. Inspection checklist items include presence of employees at the registered address, original labor contracts, dispatch agreements, employer's liability insurance evidence, payroll ledger, social insurance contribution records, office equipment and signage, and conformity of the business name plate with the license. Municipal SAMR, tax bureaus, and human resources and social security authorities may conduct coordinated onsite visits after license issuance or upon receipt of labor complaints.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR business name pre-clearance and enterprise incorporation registration (administrative fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - no official registration fee is charged for ordinary WFOE incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule; currently zero official fee, market agents may charge a service fee separately

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of parent company notarized corporate documents for five instruments plus handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin country competent authority for Apostille, or PRC Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 40 to 70 per document official fee plus translation and agency handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of parent company notarized documents and Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Qualified translation company with translation seal and translator certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 8 to 15 per Chinese page plus notarization of translation consistency

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office lease deposit and first month rent for 30 to 50 square meters in a Tier-1 city fringe area
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of RMB 4 to 6 per square meter per day in suburban Tier-1 office parks; deposit usually equal to two months rent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of WFOE Articles of Association, shareholder resolutions, and pre-incorporation application dossier review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 300 to 500 per hour or fixed fee for pre-incorporation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Human Resources Service License and Labor Dispatch Administrative License preliminary application and compliance consulting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm or HRO compliance consultant and local government application fee pass-through, if any
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed engagement fee per license; government fees, if charged by county-level SAMR or human resources authorities, are nominal and passed through at cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO filing system setup and PEP and sanctions screening subscription for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data vendor and external AML/CFT compliance adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual license fee for SME sanctions screening tool plus implementation consulting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account pre-opening documentation and bank interview support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local corporate bank for free application and external counsel for onboarding document preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for document preparation and attendance at the bank interview

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Chapter II on Incorporation and Organizational Structure of Limited Liability Companies and related articles on registered capital, articles of association, legal representative, board of directors, supervisor and filing duties; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 3, 6, 8, 12, 31 and 41; Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Market Entities; Regulations on the Administration of Human Resources Market; Regulations on Labor Dispatch; and State Administration for Market Regulation implementing rules on foreign-invested enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), with registration executed by the local Municipal or District-level Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the integrated one-stop enterprise registration online portal of the local government.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form filed together with the Articles of Association, shareholder resolutions, legal representative and supervisor appointment documents, and the Foreign Investment Information Report; the approved instrument is issued as the Business License for Enterprise Legal Person with a Unified Social Credit Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital is applicable to an ordinary wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company under PRC law as long as it does not enter a restricted or licensed sector; the registered capital amount is set by the shareholder in the Articles of Association. Under the 2023 Company Law, shareholders must fully pay subscribed capital before the expiry of five years from the date of incorporation, unless a more stringent sectoral rule applies. No escrow or blocked account requirement is imposed for a staffing agency under foreign investment law. However, if the WFOE provides labor dispatch services on the Chinese mainland, the Labor Dispatch Administrative License requires registered capital of not less than RMB 2,000,000 and a capital verification report confirming the paid-in amount. Foreign exchange capital contributions must be remitted through a designated SAFE-registered capital account and recorded in the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD, THE COMPANY, PASSED IN WRITING ON THE DATE RECORDED IN THE COMPANY RECORDS PURSUANT TO THE COMPANY LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA AND THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. PRESENT AT THE FORMATION OF THE MEETING WERE ALL DIRECTORS DULY APPOINTED BY THE FOREIGN SOLE SHAREHOLDER. NOTICE AND QUORUM REQUIREMENTS WERE WAIVED AND THE DIRECTORS ACTED UNANIMOUSLY. 1. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED THAT THE STATUTORY REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE LOCATED AT THE ADDRESS IDENTIFIED IN THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION, BEING A LAWFULLY LEASED AND SUITABLE DOMICILE FOR CORPORATE AND REGULATORY PURPOSES. THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE AND THE GENERAL MANAGER ARE AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE THE LEASE, TO PROCURE THE REGISTERED OFFICE USE DECLARATION, TO PAY RENT AND DEPOSITS, AND TO FILE THE DOMICILE CONFIRMATION WITH THE ADMINISTRATION FOR MARKET REGULATION. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED THAT THE SHAREHOLDER'S SUBSCRIPTION TO THE REGISTERED CAPITAL SET OUT IN THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION IS CONFIRMED AND ACCEPTED. THE SHAREHOLDER SHALL MAKE ALL CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE AGREED CONTRIBUTION SCHEDULE AND WITH THE BANKING, FOREIGN EXCHANGE, SOCIAL INSURANCE AND CAPITAL VERIFICATION REQUIREMENTS OF THE STATE ADMINISTRATION FOR FOREIGN EXCHANGE AND OTHER COMPETENT AUTHORITIES. THE DIRECTORS ARE AUTHORIZED TO MAINTAIN THE REGISTER OF MEMBERS, TO CAUSE SHARE CERTIFICATES TO BE ISSUED UPON FULL PAYMENT, AND TO RECORD ALL CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS IN THE COMPANY'S ACCOUNTING RECORDS. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED THAT A CORPORATE CURRENT ACCOUNT SHALL BE OPENED WITH THE BANK SELECTED BY MANAGEMENT AT ITS DESIGNATED BRANCH. ANY ONE OF THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE, THE GENERAL MANAGER OR THE CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER MAY SIGN FOR OPERATIONAL PAYMENTS NOT EXCEEDING THE INTERNAL APPROVAL LIMIT, WHILE ANY TWO OF THE AUTHORIZED SIGNATORIES, OR THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE JOINTLY WITH THE CHAIRMAN, SHALL SIGN FOR PAYMENTS ABOVE THE LIMIT, BANK FINANCING DOCUMENTS, GUARANTEES, PLEDGES AND OTHER SECURED TRANSACTIONS. THE BANK IS AUTHORIZED TO HONOR ALL INSTRUCTIONS, CHEQUES, WIRES AND DIRECT DEBITS IN CONFORMITY WITH THIS RESOLUTION AND WITH THE LOCAL PAYROLL AND CROSS-BORDER PAYMENT RAILS APPROVED FOR USE. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED THAT THE BOARD APPOINTS THE NOMINEES TO OFFICE AS CHAIRMAN, LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE AND GENERAL MANAGER, AND SUPERVISOR, WITH THE POWERS AND DUTIES PRESCRIBED BY LAW AND THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE IS AUTHORIZED TO SIGN THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION, REGISTRATION APPLICATIONS, LICENSING APPLICATIONS, TAX AND SOCIAL SECURITY FORMS, BANK INSTRUCTIONS AND ALL DOCUMENTS REQUIRED TO GIVE EFFECT TO THE INCORPORATION. 5. FURTHER ACTS. RESOLVED THAT THE DIRECTORS, THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE AND THE GENERAL MANAGER ARE AUTHORIZED TO PREPARE AND SUBMIT THE FOREIGN-INVESTED ENTERPRISE ESTABLISHMENT APPLICATION, TO APPLY FOR THE HUMAN RESOURCES SERVICE LICENSE AND, IF APPLICABLE, THE LABOR DISPATCH LICENSE, TO ENGRAVE AND USE THE COMPANY SEAL, TO REGISTER FOR TAX, SOCIAL INSURANCE, HOUSING FUND AND STATISTICS, TO APPOINT LEGAL COUNSEL AND ACCOUNTANTS, TO ENTER INTO EMPLOYMENT AND PAYROLL AGREEMENTS, AND TO DO ALL SUCH ACTS AS ARE NECESSARY OR INCIDENTAL TO GIVING EFFECT TO THE FOREGOING. THIS RESOLUTION IS EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY AND A COPY SHALL BE PROVIDED TO EVERY STATUTORY AUTHORITY, BANK AND REGISTERED AGENT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the Municipal Integrated Online Government Service Portal; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for nationwide name database coordination.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative company names together with the foreign investor identity documents through the local AMR one-stop enterprise registration portal. Before submission, screen the latest Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access, commonly called the Negative List, to confirm that human resources and employer-of-record staffing services are within the permitted scope for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. The submission must include a negative-list self-declaration and a notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized copy of the foreign investor corporate registration certificate and investor resolution. If the proposed name is accepted, the AMR issues a name reservation notice and assigns a reservation validity period; no administrative filing fee is charged for this step.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name list with at least three alternatives
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation or equivalent registration document, notarized at source and apostilled or consular-legalized
Board resolution or shareholder resolution of the foreign investor approving the China WFOE incorporation
Power of attorney appointing the local registration representative
Negative List compliance self-declaration
Passport or identity copies of proposed directors, legal representative, supervisor and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity, submit alternative names or obtain a written consent and undertaking from the prior name holder. If the Negative List screening identifies a restricted sector, revise the proposed business scope or adjust the equity structure to a permitted joint venture posture and resubmit. Where the application is suspended, respond to the AMR query within ten working days through the same portal; an administrative reconsideration or complaint is available against an unlawful refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization and Legalization of the Articles of Association and Formation Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and competent legalization authority in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction; Chinese embassy or consulate where consular legalization applies; the foreign investor's corporate registry for certificate extraction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation, the foreign sole shareholder must execute the Articles of Association in a form that satisfies Chinese company law and the local AMR registration requirements. The Articles of Association must state the company name, registered address, business scope, registered capital, contribution schedule, governance structure, legal representative, supervisor, and dissolution and liquidation rules. The shareholder signature must be supported by notarization in the home jurisdiction followed by an apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention where the jurisdiction is a member, or by consular legalization where not. A complete English-Chinese translation of the Articles of Association must be prepared with a certified translator declaration. The local registration agent should retain original documents, certified copies and translation copies for submission to the AMR in the next step.
required_dossiers: Duly executed Articles of Association for the WFOE
Notarial certificate and apostille or consular legalization of the foreign investor's registration certificate and corporate resolutions
Professional translation of the Articles of Association with translator declaration
Power of attorney for the local agent, notarized and legalized as required
Appointment letters for legal representative, directors and supervisor
Documentation showing registered office address for AMR verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a document is rejected as insufficiently legalized, cure the defect by obtaining a fresh apostille or consular legalization from the home jurisdiction and resubmit with a corrected translation. If the AMR requires further explanations, provide a supplementary written statement from the shareholder. If the registration agent identifies a conflict in the Articles of Association under Chinese law, amend the affected clause through a formal shareholder written resolution and re-execute the Articles of Association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Establishment Filing and Issuance of the Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District or Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) one-stop enterprise registration window; Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Information Reporting system where integrated with the registration platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment dossier through the AMR one-stop enterprise registration portal during the name reservation validity period. The application must include the signed Articles of Association, the establishment registration application form, foreign investor qualification documents, legal representative and supervisor appointment instruments, office premises proof, and the Negative List compliance declaration. The AMR validates the Unified Social Credit Code, business scope and statutory officer information. Upon approval, the AMR issues the Business License for Enterprise Legal Person, and the legal representative must sign the receipt and confirm the registered scope. Immediately after issuance, the foreign investor must complete the Foreign Investment Information Report online and the company must declare the relevant stamp tax and pay any statutory fees, if applicable.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form
Final executed Articles of Association
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and powers of attorney
Notarized and legalized board or shareholder resolution of the foreign investor
Office lease agreement and landlord property ownership certificate
Identity documents and appointment letters for all statutory officers
Negative List compliance declaration
Foreign Investment Information Report filing receipt after submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a query or suspend notice, respond through the online registration portal within the stated deadline and attach any missing documents. If the application is withdrawn, correct the defects and resubmit without requiring a new name reservation if the reservation remains valid. If the AMR issues a formal refusal, demand a written decision with reasons, correct the legal basis, restructure the application, and if necessary file an administrative reconsideration with the next higher AMR or initiate administrative litigation within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration, Seal Engraving, Tax, Social Security, Housing Fund and Foreign Exchange Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving agency; local State Taxation Administration tax office; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau social insurance registration center; housing fund management center; designated bank approved by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange for capital account transactions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the original Business License, arrange the engraving of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal at a Public Security Bureau-approved engraving office. Then register the company for tax within thirty days of the license issuance, complete social insurance registration for employers, register for housing fund, and activate the electronic tax invoice system. The foreign investor must open a foreign currency capital account at a designated bank, complete SAFE foreign investment registration, and after actual remittance of capital record the contribution and obtain a capital verification report where required by the applicable license. The company must also execute the banking mandate adopted by the board resolution and connect the permitted payroll payment rails, including local payroll direct debit and Wise, using the designated corporate current account.
required_dossiers: Original Business License with Unified Social Credit Code
Legal representative and general manager identity documents
Company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal engraving approval and stamp specimen
Articles of Association and board resolution on banking authority
Tax registration application forms and lease contract
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
SAFE registration application with foreign investor certificate
Capital remittance instruction and bank account opening documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, submit a supplemental registration online, pay any late-filing penalties and preserve evidence of the currency of the underlying obligations. If the social insurance registration is queried, correct employee headcount declarations and re-submit within five working days. If SAFE rejects the capital account filing, correct the foreign investment information report and coordinate with the designated bank; a fresh board resolution or amended Articles of Association may be required to align the account mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Licensing for Human Resources Service and Labor Dispatch Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSSB) under the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS); local window or online administrative licensing platform of the relevant municipal government.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing any human resources intermediary, recruitment, staffing or labor dispatch activity on the Chinese mainland, the WFOE must apply to the local HRSSB for the Human Resources Service Administrative License. If the business model includes placing employees with client employers as a labor dispatch arrangement, the company must also obtain the Labor Dispatch Administrative License. The licensing application must describe the business scope, workplace, service procedures, labor contract templates, payroll and social insurance processes, and internal compliance rules. For labor dispatch, the company must demonstrate paid-in registered capital of not less than RMB 2,000,000, submit a capital verification report, fixed premises certificate and dispatch management systems. The HRSSB will review the dossiers and may conduct an on-site inspection before issuing the licenses. Pure international employer-of-record payroll processing for foreign entities may require only the human resources license or no local license, but that scope must be verified with the local HRSSB.
required_dossiers: Standard application form for Human Resources Service Administrative License
Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Articles of Association and corporate governance documents
Certificate of fixed office premises and lease contract
Human resources service rules and complaint handling procedures
Labor dispatch management rules, contract templates and social insurance procedures where labor dispatch license is requested
Capital verification report showing paid-in registered capital of at least RMB 2,000,000 for labor dispatch license
Identity documents and professional qualification statements of the proposed managers and service staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the HRSSB asks for additional information, respond within the statutory cure period with corrected documents and an explanation. If the labor dispatch license is refused because capital is not fully paid, make the required contribution and submit an updated capital verification report before re-filing. If a license is denied, request the written refusal reasons and file an administrative reconsideration or administrative lawsuit if the denial is unlawful. The company shall not advertise staffing or dispatch services until the applicable license is actually granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSSB) under the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS); no municipal industrial manufacturing authority applies because ISIC 7810 is an office-based employment services activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Human Resources Service Administrative License for the employer-of-record, recruitment and human resources intermediary business; additionally, the Labor Dispatch Administrative License if the WFOE carries on labor dispatch activities under Chinese labor law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no construction or industrial project is undertaken; the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and its provincial ecology bureaus have no licensing role for this pure staffing and employer-of-record service company.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - an EIA registration, EIA report form or full EIA report is not required for a non-industrial office-based entity under the List of Classified Management of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the WFOE will not operate regulated wastewater outfalls, VOC-emitting industrial processes or hazardous waste storage. Domestic sanitary wastewater is discharged to the municipal sewer network, and office solid waste is collected by municipal sanitation services. No quantified emission or discharge limit applies; this conclusion must be revisited only if a separate physical training center, warehouse or manufacturing facility is later added to the business scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No high-tier Civil Defense fire permit is applicable because there is no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing facility. For the leased commercial office, the landlord must provide the building-level Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate and the company must maintain basic fire safety equipment, evacuation plans, fire extinguishers and emergency lighting. If the WFOE undertakes interior fit-out requiring construction filing, a simplified fire safety filing or acceptance notification with the local housing and urban-rural construction authority may be required before occupancy. Occupational clearance is limited to general workplace safety obligations under the Work Safety Law; desk-based staffing and payroll employees require no special occupational license, but the company must adopt safe working procedures, provide labor contracts and register employees for social insurance and work injury insurance through the local social security system.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); administered through provincial and municipal tax service bureaus and the national Electronic Tax Bureau platform at etax.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a China-established WFOE, the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code issued by the Administration for Market Regulation is the statutory taxpayer identification number and VAT identification number. Purchase the business license through the integrated one-stop registration system; the tax authority obtains the registration record electronically. Within 30 days of the AMR business license issuance, complete taxpayer onboarding on the Electronic Tax Bureau by real-name authentication, confirmation of tax categories, VAT taxpayer status election, withholding registration, and banking information filing. Non-resident entities without a Chinese permanent establishment must register for a non-resident enterprise tax identification number at the competent tax authority through the withholding agent or by direct application under the State Taxation Administration's non-resident tax registration measures; the same number is used for Enterprise Income Tax withholding and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is a Chinese tax-resident limited liability company taxed on its worldwide income at entity level, with no pass-through recognition, branch attribution not available, and distributions to foreign shareholders subject to withholding tax under the applicable double tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; China does not provide US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. VAT elections are available: a small-scale taxpayer whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed RMB 5,000,000 may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer with input credit entitlement; an entity with projected turnover above the statutory threshold must register as a general taxpayer. Hybrid mismatch treatment follows STA anti-avoidance circulars rather than taxpayer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for WFOE VAT registration: every entity holding an AMR business license is automatically registered for VAT through the multi-license integration mechanism. The compulsory general VAT taxpayer threshold is annual taxable turnover above RMB 5,000,000. Below this amount, small-scale taxpayer status applies unless an election is made. The EOR/staffing platform services are generally subject to the 6% modern-services VAT rate; the 13% rate applies to the sale of goods and is the statutory headline rate; cross-border exports can be 0% where statutory conditions are met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA has rolled out fully digitalised electronic invoices through the national Digital Electronic Invoice Service Platform. FDEI are issued, transmitted, and stored entirely electronically; each invoice carries a unified national invoice number, a dynamic anti-fraud QR code, and is cleared in real time through the STA central system. Taxpayers using conventional VAT invoice management must transmit invoice data through authorised tax-control equipment or the electronic tax bureau API at the time of issuance. Third-party invoicing software must use the STA-approved interfaces; real-time reporting failure or failure to pass anti-fraud verification can block invoice issuance and trigger tax audit alerts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For exported goods, the VAT rate is zero when the goods are physically exported from mainland China through customs supervision and the export declaration is filed by the WFOE; the taxpayer is entitled to export tax rebate on the corresponding input VAT. For cross-border services, a 0% rate applies only to the specific zero-rated cross-border taxable services enumerated in Caishui [2016] No. 36 Annex 4 and subsequent STA announcements, such as offshore service outsourcing activities, where the recipient is an overseas entity and the relevant service is wholly consumed outside mainland China. EOR payroll administration and staffing agency services must be supported by evidence that the labour and payroll services are carried out overseas and not used in China; where not enumerated as zero-rated, they may be exempt from VAT rather than zero-rated, and an export refund of input VAT is not automatic.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (Customs Export Declaration with export supervision status and customs release chop) evidencing the physical export from mainland China
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document proving goods delivery at the foreign destination and the overseas consignee's receipt
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate or bank receipt/SAFE foreign-exchange receipt record evidencing settlement of the sale proceeds in convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and refund claims are subject to post-clearance audit by the STA, customs, and SAFE. If the export declaration, logistics documents, or foreign-exchange receipts are false, missing, or inconsistent, the STA will disallow the repayment, claw back the refunded VAT, add late-payment surcharge, and impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded under the Tax Administration Law. Fraudulent export-refund claims are criminal offences under the Criminal Law, and the taxpayer may lose export-tax-refund status, be downgraded in customs credit management, and face unlimited retroactive assessment for wilful misstatement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a regulated convertible currency system for residents. Current account items, including service trade fees and dividend remittances, are generally convertible and no longer require administrative approval; however, they remain subject to the SAFE trade authenticity verification framework, under which each bank transaction must be supported by commercial contracts, invoices, customs declarations where applicable, or relevant service completion evidence. Capital account items, including inbound foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, and overseas securities investment, are subject to registration, filing, or prior approval by SAFE or PBOC. Foreign-invested enterprises must complete FDI registration in the SAFE system before receiving equity proceeds. Once received, foreign currency capital cannot be freely deployed; conversion into Renminbi requires a capital settlement plan and requires matching each settled amount to a bona fide operating expense. Export proceeds from services such as global employer of record must be repatriated to a domestic designated bank account within the verification window; no mandatory surrender percentage is imposed, meaning the enterprise may retain the foreign currency balances at a licensed bank. Profit remittance to offshore shareholders is recognized as a current account item but is historically conditioned on audited financial statements, corporate resolution approval, proof of tax payment and a valid tax clearance certificate, and a bank review of the FDI registration. Therefore, treasury operations need to maintain a dual-track record-keeping system for SAFE and tax authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE current account verification procedures, export receipts and cross-border service fees including EOR payroll service income must be repatriated to the entity's domestic foreign exchange account within the generally applicable statutory collection window of 90 days from the underlying export declaration or the date on which the service is rendered and invoiced. The bank will match each receipt against export verification data via the SAFE system and may request supporting trade or service contracts. No mandatory conversion ratio is imposed by the current regulatory framework; the enterprise is free to retain the foreign currency in a foreign exchange settlement account or sell it to the designated bank. Any overdue receipt without an approved derogation will be flagged to SAFE, potentially leading to a downgrade of the enterprise's foreign exchange verification grade, suspension of automatic closing, or enhanced documentary inspection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Operational Settlement Account and Capital Escrow Account
RMB Operating Currency Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and RMB Current Account
Basic Deposit Account and Foreign Exchange Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is Not Viable. Mainland China is not within the Wise or Revolut direct license network; these institutions do not hold a PBOC payment institution license or SAFE cross-border RMB license. Chinese commercial entities are required to conduct cross-border collections and payments through designated banks that interface with the SAFE digital monitoring system. Using an offshore EMI for settlement of WFOE payroll or trade proceeds would constitute an unlawful foreign exchange channel, triggering administrative penalties of 20 to 30 percent of the illegal amount and potential loss of the enterprise's FDI verification status. A hybrid structure is possible only for payments to foreign contractors outside China where the WFOE establishes a separately licensed foreign subsidiary or co-employer in that jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC rules require the WFOE's legal representative to complete a KYC interview before the corporate account is activated. Many tier-1 Chinese banks allow a remote video interview for non-resident legal representatives, but the bank's head-office anti-money laundering committee may require an in-person appearance at the local branch for higher risk industries. For staffing and EOR models, the low-risk rating usually permits a remote interview combined with a notarized power of attorney and apostilled or consular-certified passport copy. Some banks also permit consular proxy opening, wherein the representative visits the Chinese consulate or embassy in their country to have the signing authority and passport verified before sending the account-opening documents to the Chinese branch. The final decision rests with the bank's compliance unit and is not a statutory right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection from a low-tax jurisdiction parent with no operational substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain of corporate documents including parent certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, audited financial statements for two years, source-of-funds report from an international CPA firm, proof that the parent has active EOR operations and at least ten full-time employees, a tax residency certificate from the parent jurisdiction, and an undertaking not to use any bearer share or nominee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border disbursements to individual foreign contractors in multiple currencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete EOR service agreement with each client, contractor KYC forms with passport copies, beneficial ownership declarations, signed contractor agreements confirming employment or independent contractor status, payroll register with date-stamped invoices, and documentary evidence that each distribution is supported by a specific employment contract and tax withholding obligation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account proceeds converted into RMB and later used for non-operating purposes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A committed capital settlement plan pre-approved by the bank's SAFE officer, general ledger and bank statements showing settlement moneys are only used for payroll, rent, tax payments, and platform software licenses, an annual capital-account verification report by a Chinese registered accountant, and confirmation from the external auditor that no settlement proceeds were applied to securities, real estate, or non-current asset purchases without SAFE approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ambiguity due to multi-layer holding structure and offshore trust
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified UBO register with the name, nationality, residential address, and control percentage of all individuals owning more than 25 percent, a sworn statement that no bearer shares or other forms of indirect ownership exist, official registry extracts from each entity in the ownership chain, tax identification numbers for all UBOs, and an independent wealth and source-of-funds letter from a regulated financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the WFOE must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or its subsidiary to the WFOE's foreign-currency capital account at a designated tier-1 commercial bank in China. The remittance instructions must carry the SAFE FDI business file number generated on the Foreign Exchange Registration of Direct Investment, and the bank will upload the transaction to the SAFE Trade and Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. The corresponding SWIFT field must clearly state FDI capital contribution and the SAFE-recognized purpose code for foreign direct investment. After receipt, if the company requires Renminbi for operating purposes, it must complete a capital account settlement through the payment-in-X procedure, where each RMB payment is directly linked to an underlying invoice or salary schedule. The bank will require a non-resident tax clearance certificate or a shareholder loan confirmation to ensure that the contribution is not taxable. A Chinese-registered certified accountant must issue a capital verification report before the industry regulator acknowledges the paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for EOR payroll and contractor settlements will be executed through SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose code for salaries and other remuneration of employees for wage remittances to non-resident individuals, and through documentary collections or commercial letters of credit when the counterparty requests binding trade documentation. Given the service nature of the EOR business, SWIFT MT103 issued by a direct participant in CNAPS or CIPS is the primary clearing rail. Each payment instruction must reference the connected service invoice, payroll register, and employment contract; the bank will verify the transaction against the WFOE's SAFE current account records. For settlement of local payroll in RMB, payments will clear through the People's Bank of China's high-value payment system and the local settlement network. For cross-border payments to agents, a trade-related letter of credit may be issued, but this is rarely used for pure payroll disbursement and is mainly reserved for bulk billing to enterprise clients.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts, being onshore Renminbi forward settlement and sale instruments executed through licensed Chinese designated banks
Foreign exchange swap transactions between CNY and USD or between CNY and EUR
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched long-term foreign currency debt exposure, subject to prior SAFE or PBOC registration
Currency options traded on the interbank market in the name of the WFOE for genuine hedging demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Report Audit and Certified Audit Opinion (PRC Company Law statutory audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: PRC-registered certified public accounting firm; audited statements filed as annexes to SAMR annual report and STA annual CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30 for shareholder approval; in all cases on or before May 31 for CIT final settlement and before June 30 for the NECIPS annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a PRC CPA or to attach audited statements invalidates the annual report and CIT settlement; company and responsible officer face RMB 10,000-100,000 administrative fines; continuous failure triggers abnormal-list placement and ultimately administrative license revocation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined Enterprise Annual Report on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via NECIPS, with data shared to MOFCOM, STA, SAFE and the National Bureau of Statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of the calendar year after the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing causes placement on the Operation Abnormal List; three consecutive years without rectification triggers the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List and potential administrative revocation/forfeiture of the business license; fines of RMB 10,000-100,000 apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return (CIT annual return) with Audited Financial Statement Attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the competent local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from June 1; administrative penalty of 0.5-3 times the underpaid tax; separate RMB 2,000-10,000 filing penalty; enforced collection, bank attachment and VAT invoice restriction for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Direct Investment annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and local commerce departments under the Foreign Investment Law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of the following calendar year, integrated with the NECIPS annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification order followed by fine of RMB 100,000-500,000 for the enterprise and RMB 10,000-100,000 for the responsible legal representative or actual controller if the report is refused or materially false

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Labor Dispatch Agency Annual Operation Report (annual report of the administrative license holder)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (MHRSS) that granted the labor dispatch administrative license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each year for the prior calendar year in most provincial MHRSS regimes; provincial notice may fix a narrower window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning and correction order; serious or repeated failure may lead to license suspension or revocation, prohibition on new dispatch/EOR contracts, and fines of RMB 10,000-50,000 for illegal dispatch

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Shareholder Approval of Audited Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders'/members' meeting; minutes, register audit certificate and audit opinion kept in the minute book and made available for SAMR and MOFCOM inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before May 31 following fiscal year-end, and continuously updated thereafter; share transfers, director changes and charge creation must be registered within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or falsified registers invalidate capital-change filings and expose the company to fines of RMB 10,000-500,000 and responsible officers to RMB 5,000-100,000 under the Company Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Contribution Base Declaration and Payroll Confirmation for Staffing/EOR Workforce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local social insurance administration and the local tax bureau exercising delegated collection authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Provincial deadline generally falling between June 1 and July 31 for the current contribution base; exact date is published annually by the local MHRSS/tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imputed contribution base and daily late-payment fee of 0.05%; administrative penalty of 0.5-3 times unpaid contributions; denial of social-insurance proof may block payroll, visa and foreign-exchange compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law (2023), every limited company, including a WFOE, is required to appoint a PRC-registered CPA to audit its annual financial report; this universal status-based mandate has no size exemption. For regulatory filing purposes, complete audited financial statements and an independent audit opinion must accompany the SAMR annual report and STA final settlement where (i) total assets at year-end reach or exceed RMB 40 million, (ii) annual operating revenue reaches or exceeds RMB 30 million, or (iii) headcount reaches or exceeds 300 employees. A global EOR/staffing agency under ISIC 7810/NAICS 561330 will normally trigger the turnover and headcount thresholds. Licensed labor-dispatch agencies and financial/investment licensees are audited irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), substantially converged with IFRS; audits are performed under Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSA); small non-public enterprises may use Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises only when not required to provide consolidated/group reporting or audited foreign-investment settlement data

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not operate a separate public UBO register; the controlling shareholder and actual controller information is confirmed annually through the combined NECIPS/MOFCOM annual report. Every shareholding transfer or actual-controller change must be filed with SAMR within 30 days and recorded contemporaneously in the company's internal register of members. At the annual shareholders' meeting the board shall confirm the UBO/actual-controller structure and produce a signed register audit certificate before the statutory audit opinion is released. Continuous non-disclosure triggers abnormal-list placement, fines and restrictions on new registrations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500-6,000 per year for a shared office/registered-address service in tier-2 cities; USD 8,000-25,000 per year for physical registered premises or professional agency services in Beijing, Shanghai or Shenzhen
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-18,000 per year for a WFOE with cross-border payroll, intercompany recharges and 50-1,000 contractor files; complex multi-entity or listed-parent groups may be higher

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A China-incorporated WFOE is a resident enterprise chargeable at the 25% headline Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate. Applicable incentives include: (a) qualified Small Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million may enjoy an effective 5% EIT rate; (b) High and New Technology Enterprises pay 15%; (c) certain software and integrated-circuit enterprises may obtain two-year exemption and three-year half-rate treatment; (d) eligible R&D expenses are super-deductible at 100%; China does not maintain a traditional patent box, but qualified technology transfer income may be partially exempt under specific EIT incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A Class; main form A100000 and supporting schedules) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax portal. Quarterly provisional returns and withholding returns for non-resident payments are filed on the same e-tax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement plus quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly EIT prepayments must be paid within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The annual EIT return and final settlement must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e. by 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE. Withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest and royalties to non-residents is governed by a separate 7-day remittance rule after the payment occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue: gross EOR platform service fees, workforce administration fees, payroll processing fees, placement commissions and all directly billed contractor fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must report worldwide income in China. For a global EOR model, payroll pass-through receipts must not simply be netted against client payments unless the WFOE is contractually and physically a disclosed payment agent. All connected-party service revenue must be booked at arm's length and, where the non-resident parent bears part of the contract risk, only the remunerated scope should be recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total cost of sales / principal operating costs: employee wages, social insurance, housing fund, benefits, and subcontract staffing costs incurred to deliver the EOR service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduction is allowed only where the WFOE can evidence employment or valid service contracts, payroll settlement records, social security declarations, bank transfer proof and invoices. Costs paid to global contractors through non-banking rails without receipts may be disallowed, and classification as dividend or remuneration to non-resident providers may trigger additional withholding and transfer pricing risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and supplementary P&L items: selling, administrative and financial expenses, asset impairment losses, fair-value gains/losses and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border management fees, IT charges, headquarters allocations and intercompany royalties are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, the WFOE receives an economic benefit, no duplicate charge exists, and the amount is arm's length. If the foreign parent charges at zero markup or inflated prices, the tax authority may apply special tax adjustment and impose deemed interest on underpaid tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit: calculated as total revenue less total costs, expenses, taxes and impairment adjustments shown in earlier rows.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile this line to audited financial statements. If the WFOE's cross-border service margin is lower than its functional and risk profile would justify, the examiner will propose a TNMM or bilateral adjustment. The WFOE should retain full transfer pricing documentation for the EOR delivery chain, including country-by-country records of workers and payroll funding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and non-operating expenditure: asset disposal gains, penalties, donations, exchange differences and similar one-off items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible payments to non-residents such as fines, bribes, or unverified compensation must be added back. Interest-free or artificially low-interest loans from the non-resident parent create deemed interest income for the lender and may be recharacterized as additional taxable income of the WFOE where the benefit is shifted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: applies tax law adjustments, adds non-deductible amounts, subtracts exempt and adjusted items, and applies the prior-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE operating global EOR business, loss carryforward is limited to five years for general taxpayers and ten years for qualified high-tech and small technology enterprises. Losses from foreign branches or shell subsidiaries cannot be offset against China-sourced EOR income unless the entity has genuine substance and the attribution is supported by local documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final EIT calculation: headline rate, preferential rate, tax payable, tax credits, overseas income tax and foreign tax credit, then net amount due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate or documented preferential rate. If the WFOE receives dividends or profits from its offshore EOR affiliates, a foreign tax credit can be claimed through the relevant schedule. Distributions by the WFOE to its non-resident parent are not taxed on this EIT return; instead the payer must withhold non-resident dividend tax and file a separate withholding return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return attracts an administrative penalty of RMB 2,000-10,000; late payment accrues a surcharge of 0.05% per day on the overdue tax. Understatement or evasion of EIT can result in a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. If the amount evaded is significant and represents more than 10% of tax payable for the corresponding period, criminal liability may arise under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to seven years and fines. Failure to keep contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation carries additional penalties under the tax administration rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise holding shares, unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Arrangement (DTA/DTA economy).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must apply for treaty benefits before the dividend remittance is executed. The administrative protocol requires: (i) submission of the treaty benefit declaration form to the Chinese payer's competent tax authority, typically through the electronic withholding system; (ii) provision of a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) or equivalent certificate issued by the jurisdiction of residence covering the dividend year; (iii) written evidence of beneficial ownership, including audited financial statements, board resolutions, ultimate shareholder register, and an explanation that the recipient is not a conduit or agent; (iv) confirmation that the parent company has substance and bears economic risk; and (v) if the Hong Kong arrangement is invoked, a formal residency attestation and treaty-specific claim form. The reduced 5% dividend rate under the Mainland-Hong Kong arrangement requires direct ownership of at least 25% of the WFOE's capital and satisfaction of all beneficial ownership tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% each under the PRC EIT Law. Under the PRC-Hong Kong Arrangement, interest may fall to 7% and royalties to 5% (with 10% applying to certain film/copyright royalties) where beneficial ownership exists. Other Chinese income tax treaties frequently reduce interest and royalty WHT to 0%-10%, but anti-treaty-shopping rules, thin-capitalisation limits and the Principal Purpose Test must all be satisfied before the reduced rate is applied to intercompany debt and intellectual property charges.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China's contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation thresholds require a Local File when related-party tangible-asset transfers exceed RMB 200 million, intangible-asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, financial-asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, or services/other related-party transactions exceed RMB 40 million in a tax year. A Master File is required when total related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion in the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not impose Guernsey-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the tax authorities apply the broader substance-over-form doctrine, controlled-foreign-company rules and the general anti-avoidance rule under EIT Law Article 47. A WFOE operating a global EOR platform must demonstrate that its core income-generating activities (CIGA), including client contracting, payroll administration, social insurance filings, invoicing, treasury operations and risk decisions, are performed and managed in China. The OECD Multilateral Instrument's Principal Purpose Test, applicable to China's covered tax agreements, allows denial of treaty benefits where the offshore parent or intermediate holding entity lacks real commercial substance and was interposed mainly to obtain treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and False Payroll Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE understates gross EOR revenue by treating payroll pass-through as non-taxable, uses fake worker identities or back-to-back contracts to inflate salary expense, claims social insurance costs without real contributions, or purchases fabricated special VAT invoices to create artificial deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Administration Law Article 63, tax evasion carries a penalty of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax, daily late-payment surcharges at 0.05%, and recovery of all overdue tax. Under Criminal Law Article 201, deliberate concealment of taxable income constituting a significant amount and more than 10% of payable tax is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment up to three years; where the amount is enormous, imprisonment of three to seven years and fines may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director manages the WFOE and shareholder assets indistinguishably, personally signs false invoices, or directs diversion of EOR payroll funds. Directors and de facto controllers may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax from personal assets, subjected to asset preservation orders, travel bans, restricted consumption orders and blacklisting as dishonest judgment debtors under Supreme People's Court rules, and may receive custodial sentences under the criminal tax provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Deficient TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE charges its non-resident parent or affiliates artificially low service fees for EOR contract performance, leaves the parent with only fiscal effects but no functional substance, allocates group management fees without controlling benefit, fails to prepare the China Local File or Master File when the statutory thresholds are exceeded, or manipulates intercompany loans and royalty payments to strip Chinese profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 44, when contemporaneous documentation is absent, the tax authority may determine taxable income by deemed profit methods, resulting in additional tax, penalties and a five-year special-interest charge on underpaid tax. Tax Administration Law Article 45 imposes fines up to RMB 10,000 for documentation failures; where the mispricing amounts to evasion, the 50%-500% evasion penalty and Criminal Law Article 201 apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false related-party transaction schedules, control non-arm's length pricing committees, or order incomplete books can be held personally liable for the resulting corporate tax and interest where the corporate form was misused. Courts may garnish the director's domestic bank accounts, prohibit departure from China, blacklist the director under civil enforcement measures, and in fraud cases impose imprisonment up to three years; repeated multi-entity schemes can attract longer custodial terms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and AML Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is formed as a shell with no physical office, staff, bank account or revenue-generating substance and is interposed between mainland clients and an offshore group solely to invoice EOR services, pay outbound dividends/royalties to a low-tax jurisdiction, or claim a lower dividend withholding rate under a tax treaty that was not objectively available to the true beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 47 and the Principal Purpose Test in China's covered tax treaties, the tax authority may disregard the intermediary entity, re-source the income to the beneficial owner, deny treaty benefits, impose the statutory 10% withholding tax plus interest and penalties under the Tax Administration Law. Where the operation conceals the identity of ultimate beneficial owners or processes illicit funds, the anti-money laundering regime permits fines against the entity, responsible officers and persons in charge, and Criminal Law Article 191 imposes fines and imprisonment for money laundering offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and actual controllers of a zombie WFOE may have the corporate veil pierced if they commingle the entity's funds with parent assets, use the WFOE bank account to receive unlawful payments, or structure the entity to avoid consolidation. Under PRC Company Law the controlling shareholder who causes confusion with corporate assets is personally liable for company debts. The director may be subject to asset restitution, travel restrictions, entry of the name into the social credit blacklist, seizure of personal property and criminal imprisonment up to seven years for laundering the proceeds of substantive tax evasion.
